$comment: What this site may no longer claim.
IAES 2.0 withdrew the ISO 13374 attributions and stopped describing its ISO
citations as alignment: the correspondences had never been verified against
the cited documents. That decision was made in the standard's repository.
This site kept publishing the withdrawn claims -- in seven surfaces and, for
the ones that live in i18n.js, in fourteen languages.
The site needs mechanical memory of what it can no longer say, because prose
has no schema and a person re-adding a phrase months from now will not
remember an RFC. tools/check_withdrawn_claims.py reads this file.
This file is NOT authority over IAES. It records what the specification
already decided, and cites where. If the two ever disagree, the
specification governs -- GOVERNANCE.md 2.
Two kinds of entry, because the two need different tests:
phrases  English wording that asserts the withdrawn claim. Checked in
HTML and in the English block of i18n.js, where the source text
lives.
keys     i18n keys whose whole purpose was to carry a withdrawn claim.
Checked by NAME across every language, because a regex for an
English phrase cannot find its Japanese translation. Retiring the
key retires all fourteen at once.

withdrawn.authority: IAES_SPEC.md, References -- ISO 14224, 17359, 13374 series and 55000 are all 'Normative for meaning: No'
withdrawn.why: Citation is not alignment. Naming a standard for context does not make an event conform to it.
The site claimed a field-level mapping to four standards. No such correspondence was ever verified against the documents, and three of the four were never held.
phrases: maps its event types and fields directly

withdrawn.authority: IAES_SPEC.md Appendix C -- 'carries a health status level from IAES's own vocabulary. The attribution to ISO 13374-2 was withdrawn in 2.0'
withdrawn.why: The seven iso_13374_status values are IAES's own. The field name is kept for 1.x compatibility and attributes nothing.

withdrawn.authority: ISO 13374-4:2015 captions the block diagram 'from ISO 13374-1:2003'; ISO 13374-2:2007 is a five-layer information architecture
withdrawn.why: The six-block model is part 1, not part 2. The site must not repeat the specification's own misattribution while RFC-009 is open.

allowed.text: IAES: An Open, ISO-Aligned Event Standard for Industrial Asset Intelligence
allowed.why: The title of a preprint published with a DOI. It is immutable and citing it accurately is not making the claim -- the same distinction GOVERNANCE.md 1.1 draws between attribution and dependency. The link must carry the note that the title predates 2.0.

allowed.text: Earlier IAES material used the phrase “ISO-aligned” and described a field-level mapping to those four documents. IAES 2.0 withdrew those claims where the correspondence had not been verified against the cited document. Nothing about the wire format changed: the fields kept their names and their values, and what changed is what is asserted about them.
allowed.why: The page that explains the withdrawal has to be able to name what was withdrawn. Exempting the sentence rather than the page keeps the licence narrow: edit this sentence and the exemption stops matching, which the guard reports rather than silently widening.
